subject: Notice: Elevated P95 latency & temporary routing backoff — RiverPoint
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@riverpoint.com>, RiverPoint Engineering <ops@riverpoint.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Elevated P95 latency & temporary routing backoff — RiverPoint

Hi Elena / RiverPoint team,

I wanted to let you know we observed a sustained elevation in p95 response times for a subset of your traffic to our hosted inference endpoint (api.redwood.com/v1/generate) starting ~08:45 PDT. We’ve opened an ops bridge and taken the following actions to limit customer impact: 

- Activated a routing backoff policy for affected regions to direct new requests to a compatible model variant with larger headroom.
- Enabled prefix-level KV caching for hot prefixes seen in RiverPoint traffic.
- Temporarily reduced batch window for RiverPoint pool to prioritize tail latency.

Status page & incident: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/RW-2026-05-17
We expect the routing mitigation to significantly reduce p95 within ~30 minutes; we’ll post updates to the status page.

Could you confirm if you are seeing an increase in error rate or any client-side timeouts? If so, a short access log (top 5 request IDs) would help us correlate.

Attachment: incident-snapshot-20260517.png (small latency histogram)

Apologies for the interruption — we’re prioritizing this and I’ll keep you posted.

– Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147
From: Elena Morales <elena@riverpoint.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: Elevated P95 latency & temporary routing backoff — RiverPoint

Thanks for the heads up, Karthik.

We are seeing increased p95 on our side, a few clients have reported slow responses to our UI. No increase in 5xx errors reported yet, but one customer timed out at 10s. I’ve attached a quick snippet of the client-side log and 3 request IDs: rp-20260517-3101, rp-20260517-3114, rp-20260517-3140.

Please let us know if you need anything else. We’ll keep our SRE on watch.

– Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, RiverPoint Analytics
elena@riverpoint.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@riverpoint.com>, RiverPoint Engineering <ops@riverpoint.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: Elevated P95 latency & temporary routing backoff — RiverPoint

Elena — thanks for the IDs. We’ve correlated rp-20260517-3114 and rp-20260517-3140 to high queuing on the primary hosting pool. What we’ve done in the bridge: 

- Evacuated several overloaded workers from the RiverPoint pool to the low-latency fallback pool.
- Applied a targeted multiplier to rate-limit low-priority batch work for your org (non-prod calls excluded).
- Captured bridge logs and early traces; see ops-bridge-log-20260517.txt attached.

Preliminary analysis (private): seems correlated to a sudden burst of long-context requests from an ad-hoc job (identified by user-agent header). We are tracing the full KV cache hit-rate and kernel saturation metrics now.

We will keep your SRE updated every 30 minutes on progress and will post the full timeline on the incident doc once the bridge closes: https://docs.redwood.com/incident/RW-2026-05-17-analysis

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Incident Response Lead, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@riverpoint.com>, RiverPoint Engineering <ops@riverpoint.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: RW-2026-05-17 — mitigation complete & next steps

Elena / RiverPoint team,

Quick post-incident follow-up now that the bridge is closed. Summary: 

- Impact window: 2026-05-17 08:45–11:25 PDT (p95 elevated; isolated to requests with long-context tokens).
- Mitigation: routing backoff + targeted eviction of overloaded workers + prefix KV warming restored p95 to baseline by ~11:10 PDT.
- Root cause (preliminary): sudden high-cardinality long-context job from within your environment (identified by request metadata) that caused kernel-level queuing on our primary worker pool.

What we’re doing next (action plan):
1) Scheduled a joint investigation meeting Tuesday, 2026-05-19 10:00 PDT to walk logs and traces (calendar invite sent).
2) We will provide a short-term guardrail: soft rate limits on long-context requests per API key and an automatic fallback to the low-latency model variant when token length > 8k.
3) Engineering will deliver a postmortem summary and recommended client-side retry/backoff patterns by 2026-05-21.

Public status page entry has been updated: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/RW-2026-05-17
Internal analysis & artifacts: https://docs.redwood.com/incident/RW-2026-05-17-analysis

If you prefer we can expand the scope of the invite to include your data-science team — let me know. We appreciate your patience and are committed to preventing recurrence.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147
